budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director met a fence contractor and expects a quote for repairs, including missing fence topper at the little league field.
A low bidder was identified and references are being checked. The contract begins July 1 for one year with renewal options up to three years.
A survey firm was asked for a ballpark price to survey the whole park but has not responded.
A member said logging maintenance would show each park's real financial needs and support requests for more park funding.

budget_items.topic: Past water bill at Marshall Park
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled a large water bill from an undetected leak.
Beach house rental was set with an hourly rate, a minimum, a non-refundable deposit and lifeguard charges.
A request is on the Town Meeting list for Saturday; if passed, money would be available July 1 to hire a master planner.
A member cited adult soccer program registration price as an example.
The skate park group reported the amount it has raised to the select board.
A member hopes the project can be funded through grants and mentioned a park grant webinar.

decisions.decision: A quarterly maintenance update to the commission was requested, from the DPW director or via the recreation director.
Commission members will draft the maintenance policy building on the DPW bid document, with DPW input.
Maintenance issue reports from the public to go through the recreation platform, with possible parks signage.
Chair to ask town counsel about liability and leash requirements before the dog policy returns.
Marshall Park survey to be finalized, tested by members and sent out via recreation staff, schools and social media.
Meetings set for the last Wednesday of each month at 6:30, starting May 26.
Chair to ask the skate park group for a final decision on locating at Marshall Park and a timeline.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted by roll call to recommend hiring three new lifeguards and rehiring the lifeguards and beach coordinator, for the town manager and select board.
The commission approved the revised beach rental policy by roll call; the vote count was not stated.
Dog policy was deferred; the chair is to ask town counsel about liability and leash requirements before it returns.
Members will draft a parks maintenance policy building on the DPW bid document, with public issue reports to go through the recreation platform.
The Marshall Park survey is to be finalized and sent out, and meetings move to the last Wednesday of each month starting May 26.

why_it_matters: The lifeguard recommendation and the beach rental policy shape whether and how the town beach is staffed and rented this summer, and the hires still need the town manager and select board.
A logged maintenance record could show each park's actual upkeep needs, which is the evidence behind any request for more park funding.
Marshall Park planning, including a master plan funding request on the Town Meeting list, is moving toward a resident survey and a possible skate park decision.
